To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formation of radical anions of phthalocianines with various central metal atoms is accompanied by changes in molecular structure, optical and magnetic properties, and EPR spectra.
radical anions of MPc(3-) with tetraalkyammonium cation salts are obtained by reduction of metal-containing and nonmetal phthalocyaninates with sodium fluorene ketyl.

the reduction of metal phthalacyanines with sodium fluorene ketyl leads to the formation of crystalline radical anion salts with metal phthalocynines [MPc3-](-), where M= Cu(II), H(2), Sn(II) and Pb(II), V(IV) and Ti(IV).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, crystal structures, and optical and magnetic properties of salts with metal-containing and metal free phthalocyaninyl radical anions.

the formation of crystalline salts 1-11 with phthalocyaninato radical anions [MPc(2-)], [MPc(1-)](-), [MPc(0)](2-), and [MPc(·-)](-) (M = Cu(II)-H2, Sn(IV), Ti(IV), and V(IV)) and their optical and magnetic characterization.
the synthesis of radical anion salts of phthalocianine and metal phthalocianines with tetraalklylammonium cations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reduction of metal-free and metal-containing phthalocyanins is accompanied by the reduction of the Pc macrocycle, which affects the molecular structure, electronic and optical, and magnetic properties of radical anions.
the Pc ligand is reduced in 1-11, but not in 1-5, 7, 9, 11.
the reduction of the phthalocyaninato ligand to radical anions in 1-11 results in significant changes of molecular structures and optical and magnetic properties of phthalocycianine complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radical anions of the phthalocyaninates are characterized by a high degree of structural disorder.
radical anions of MPc(3-), where M is metal, and MPc(-), where M is nonmetal, are structurally, optically, and magnetically different, and their formation is accompanied by changes of the Pc ligands.
the reduction of the metal-free and metal phthalocianines is an effective way for the synthesis of new radical anion salts with the Pc ligand in the radical anion form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metal-containing and metal free phthalocyaninyl radical anions are characterized not only by a new band in the NIR range but also by a significant shift of the Q- and B bands to shorter wavelengths.

the radical anion salts with the [MPc(2-), MPc(3-), or MPc(4-)](-) (where M = Cu, Ni, Sn, Pb, Ti, V) anions can be synthesized and characterized by the single-crystal XRD, EPR, and NIR absorption spectroscopy.
the formation of radical anions in metal phthalocianines affects the Pc ligand structure and optical and magnetic properties of metal phthalocyaines.
